findings.title: The copyright year lags the site's own newest content by more than a year
findings.evidence: 1 pages show a copyright year of 2003, while the newest date signal observed anywhere in the sample is 2023 -- a gap of 20 years. Example: https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/1000-places-to-see-before-you-die_1/index.html.

evidence_detail.method: a copyright year (matched via the © symbol or the word 'copyright') compared against the newest date signal (structured data, sitemap, or Last-Modified header) found anywhere in the sample, or the audit's own crawl date if no other signal exists
evidence_detail.expected: the copyright year within a year of the site's own newest content

suggested_action.summary: Update the copyright year, ideally driven automatically from the current date rather than a hand-maintained value.
how: Generate the footer copyright year from the server's own clock at render time, so it never needs manual updating.
suggested_action.mechanism: A lagging copyright year is a weak but real signal a system may use when judging how actively a site is maintained, independent of whether the content itself is still accurate.
suggested_action.verification: Re-check the footer and confirm the year matches or exceeds the site's own newest content date.
